**Premise verified on `origin/main` @ `8a9c079`** — `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs:681`: `excludesTests: (parsed.exclude ?? []).some((pattern) => TEST_GLOB.test(pattern))` — the detector is still `exclude`-shaped and `roots`/`include` still never feeds it, so the include-omission blind spot is live as measured.

**Why held rather than promoted** — the card itself names the gating unknown: nobody has counted how many packages repo-wide sit in the `include`-shaped form, and that census decides how far the ratchet moves on the day the gate starts seeing them. A fix without the census is a repo-wide ratchet change with unknown blast radius; the gate meanwhile fails no one falsely (it under-counts, it does not block). Observation-class until someone wants the ratchet moved.

**Promotion triggers recorded**: ① the census gets run (first step of any fix, and cheap to do standalone); ② a type-error regression ships through a package the gate reported as covered (the #7312 measurement shows the mechanism, but no shipped regression yet); ③ maintainer appetite for tightening the type-coverage ratchet.

**Dedup** — #7312 (the two example apps' tsconfigs, merged fix) is the parent measurement; no open card owns the gate's detector shape.

## Premise re-verified at `origin/main` @ `e3a6f6e` before claiming

The card was filed 08-10 and graded 08-11; `main` has moved since, so I re-read rather than trusting it:

- `:681` still reads `excludesTests: (parsed.exclude ?? []).some((pattern) => TEST_GLOB.test(pattern))`. Detector unchanged.
- Control check (a零命中 would otherwise be indistinguishable from a broken scan): `countRoots` still present in the same file, 2 hits.
- Only commit on the file since filing is `78ed1f4`, an unrelated lint-prescription change.

**One thing the card predates, and it strengthens the finding rather than weakening it.** Package-level `excludesTests` is now an aggregate (`:790`):

```js
excludesTests: anyExcludesTests && testsInvoked.length === 0,
```

A package with **no `exclude` at all** has `anyExcludesTests === false`, so the aggregate is `false` regardless of what `include` does. The include-shaped package is therefore invisible at *both* levels, not just at `:681`. The dispatch carries this as a measured reading, not as the card's original framing.

## Same-file serial note — recorded now so it is not discovered later

**#7888** (`finding`, opened 2026-08-12 02:17Z: nine DEBT ledger entries sitting below their recorded ceilings) targets the **DEBT ledger in this same file**. It is `finding`-class and therefore not dispatchable today, so there is no collision this round. If the triage seat promotes it, it **serializes behind this card** — same file, and specifically an overlapping region, since a detector change that moves the ratchet will move some of the very numbers #7888 is auditing. Entered in the seat post's 热文件串行队.

**ACCEPT — PR #7921.** Reviewed against GitHub, not against the report (which never arrived on this thread — see the contract note at the end).

## Verified

- **Diff: 1 file**, `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`, +273/−72. The declared file surface held exactly — **no package `tsconfig*.json` touched**, which was the boundary that mattered here: the card changes what the gate can *see*, not what the repo declares.
- **First line `Fixes #7353`** — read personally. Correct: nothing is deliberately left outstanding, so merging should close the card.
- **Gate job conclusions read personally, not from an aggregate**: **ESLint `success`**, **TypeScript Type Check `success`**. `Check Changeset` was the only red and is the expected label route — `skip-changeset` applied (scripts-only gate change, no published package). ⛔ No empty-frontmatter changeset was added, correctly (#5471 / #4898).
- **Path surface checked before any landing action**: no `docs/adr/**`, no `.claude/skills/**`, no `skills/**`. Normal queue path.

## The ruling's hard requirement is met

Triage's promotion said *"the PR must report which packages flip status so the ratchet change is deliberate, not incidental."* The PR body carries the full table — **3 packages, 65 files, 198 raw errors**:

| package | files hidden | raw errors | shape |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `@objectstack/cli` | 56 | **188** | `include: ["src"]`, **no `exclude` at all**, 56 tests in a sibling `test/` tree |
| `@objectstack/metadata-fs` | 6 | 6 | `include: ["src/**/*"]`, all 6 tests in `test/` |
| `@objectstack/example-showcase` | 3 | 4 | `e2e/` Playwright tree unread |

And it states what does **not** move: all 19 existing TEST_DEBT packages keep the same verdict *and the same file count* (719 both ways). A ratchet change that names its own blast radius in both directions is what the ruling asked for.

**The headline is `packages/cli`: 188 raw tsc errors in a test layer that no gate, no ledger and no CI job had ever read.** The card predicted a blind spot; it turned out to be worth more than the card guessed.

## What makes this a good run rather than merely a passing one

- **The dev falsified its own first census.** Pass one said 16 packages / 422 files by treating "no `typecheck` script" as "nothing reads the tests". That is wrong — `measureDebt` runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json`, and those packages already have their tests under that config's `include`. Corrected to 3 / 65. Had it shipped uncorrected, **353 files would have moved into the ledger that means "src checks, tests are hidden"** purely because DEBT already owned them. The `accountedPrograms` second clause exists to make that impossible, and it is pinned by a self-test case naming the 353-file over-reach.
- **Reverse verification is a deleted-limb test on a *fresh* package**, not a re-run of the card's own example: a `TS2322` planted in `packages/metadata-fs/test/contract.test.ts` left `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-fs exec tsc --noEmit` **green, exit 0** and the **old** detector reporting OK, while the new detector's `--re-measure` goes **red** (`records 6 … now reports 7 (+1)`). That is the card's mechanism reproduced somewhere it had not been measured, then closed.
- **Both of my dispatch assumptions were tested rather than assumed.** The aggregate reading (`anyExcludesTests && testsInvoked.length === 0` making the hole strictly bigger) is **confirmed**. So is the PINS_CHECKED hand-off claim, with a measurement I did not ask for: **all 65 newly-visible files carry zero `@ts-expect-error` directives**, so the hand-off caught none of them — the card's "reported by neither half" is now a number, not an inference.
- **`measureTestDebt` learned the same lesson rather than being patched around it**: adding hidden files to `include` one at a time (a `e2e/**/*` glob would have billed app-showcase 6 errors from `global-setup.ts`, which is not a test), and neutralising `rootDir` — measured both ways on cli, **56 TS6059 with it kept vs 188 real errors with it neutralised**. Counting the TS6059 would have been measuring the tape measure.

## The same-file serial note paid off

The claim comment flagged **#7888** as targeting the DEBT ledger in this same file. The dev read it before writing and cross-checked: its `--re-measure` at `b9f930b` **confirms #7888's reading** — 9 entries, 273 raw errors of surplus, identical entry set — and this change moves none of them (the three new entries carry zero surplus, so 273 holds before and after).

It also found **one arithmetic error in #7888's table**: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` measures **107, not 106**; `131 → 107` is the `−24` that #7888's own surplus column and its 273 total already assume, so the `measured` cell is the typo and the total is right. Recorded here; #7888 is unaffected in substance and remains its own card.

The dev **did not post its `<!-- os-dev-report -->` comment on this thread** — the report's authoritative channel. Its session went IDLE at `review_ready` with the PR open, so the work completed; only the report write is missing. I reviewed directly from the PR instead, which the state model permits (all state lives on GitHub, and the PR body carried everything the report would have). Noting it because a successor reading this thread would otherwise find a dispatch record with no terminal report and have to reconstruct why.
